note: Ramond et al. described 12 individuals across 11 families, and Shatokhina et al. reported a single individual as the second study, summing to 13 individuals across 12 families.

evidence.text: Ramond et al. identified 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families with monoallelic TRA2B variants.

source.title: Clustered variants in the 5' coding region of TRA2B cause a distinctive neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: A total of 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families who harbored predicted loss-of-function monoallelic variants, mostly de novo, were recruited.

evidence.text: Shatokhina et al. documented a single proband as the second study of human pathogenic TRA2B variants, following the initial report of 11 families.

source.title: TRA2B Gene Splice Variant Linked to Seizures and Neurodevelopmental Delay: A Second Case Study
source.quote: However, only one study has documented this association in 11 families with pathogenic or likely pathogenic TRA2B variants. In our investigation, we report a new de novo TRA2B ... This paper represents the second investigation of pathogenic variants in the TRA2B gene in humans
